m1-t1.question: Which activity is the temporary project in the placement case?
options: Introduce and hand over a new booking process
Answer routine placement calls each day
m1-t1.explanation: The project changes the process; recurring service delivery is operations.

m1-t1.question: Which is an outcome rather than an output?
options: Fewer students need a second registration visit
m1-t1.explanation: An outcome is a change in behaviour or performance, not a produced document.

m1-t1.question: What is the forecast saving at 240 registrations if handling time falls from six to four minutes?
m1-t1.explanation: 240 × 2 = 480 minutes; divide by 60 to get eight hours.

m1-t1.question: Who should resolve a scope and funding conflict outside the team’s authority?
options: Any team member who is free
The last person to edit the plan
m1-t1.explanation: The sponsor owns authorisation and escalated trade-offs.

m1-t1.question: The pilot software is installed. Which benefit statement is defensible?
options: The output is delivered; benefits still need measurement
The entire forecast saving has been realised
All registration errors have been removed
m1-t1.explanation: Delivery is not evidence that the intended operational benefit occurred.

m1-t2.question: What makes “smooth registration” a usable acceptance criterion?
options: An observable test and an agreed threshold
Repeating the phrase in the charter
m1-t2.explanation: Acceptance requires agreed evidence, not only an aspiration.

m1-t2.question: How should an unapproved SMS feature be represented?
m1-t2.explanation: Impact and authorisation must precede commitment.

m1-t2.question: What proportion is 37 successful users out of 40?
m1-t2.explanation: 37 ÷ 40 × 100 = 92.5%; compare it with the pre-agreed target.

m1-t2.question: Who should be named beside an acceptance test?
options: Only the person who wrote the code
m1-t2.explanation: A named acceptor makes the decision route explicit.

m1-t2.question: What does an explicit exclusion achieve?
options: Proves a feature has no value
Guarantees no one requests a change
m1-t2.explanation: Exclusions clarify the baseline; valuable new work can still enter change control.

m1-t3.question: Which stakeholder needs consultation even with little formal authority?
options: A student strongly affected by accessibility barriers
m1-t3.explanation: Impact matters as well as formal influence.

m1-t3.question: In the course RACI convention, how many accountable roles should a deliverable have?
m1-t3.explanation: One accountable role makes the decision route clear.

m1-t3.question: What does Consulted mean in RACI?
options: Input is sought before the relevant decision
The person owns all project funding
The person merely receives the final notice
The person must perform every task
m1-t3.explanation: Consultation is a two-way input relationship.

m1-t3.question: What belongs in a useful meeting action record?
m1-t3.explanation: Actions need ownership and a review point.

m1-t3.question: Two distinct approvals have different owners. What is the clearest RACI treatment?
options: Ask the vendor to decide both
Name both people accountable for everything
m1-t3.explanation: Separate deliverables avoid conflating different authority boundaries.

questions.question: A sponsor celebrates an installed booking form, but repeat visits have not been measured. What should the coordinator report?
options: Output delivered; outcome and benefit remain unverified
questions.explanation: Separate delivered outputs from observed outcomes and benefits.

questions.question: A booking pilot saves two minutes for 150 cases, but staff spend two hours correcting errors. What is the net observed time saving?
questions.explanation: Gross saving is 300 minutes or five hours; subtract two hours of rework.

questions.question: A high-impact learner group has little budget authority and is absent from consultation. What is the best correction?
options: Exclude them because influence is low
Let the vendor represent them without checking
Add an accessible consultation route before acceptance
questions.explanation: Stakeholder impact and access matter independently of power.

questions.question: A charter excludes payments. A senior lecturer requests them verbally. What is the defensible response?
options: Log the request and seek impact review and authorisation
Delete the exclusion without a record
Refuse to record any new request
questions.explanation: Authority and change control apply even to valuable requests.

questions.question: Two reviewers each think the other approves launch. How should the RACI be repaired?
options: Make every consulted role the sponsor
Separate distinct approvals and name one accountable role for each
Mark all staff accountable for everything
questions.explanation: Distinct decisions need clear ownership rather than shared ambiguity.

questions.question: A user test succeeds for 46 of 50 participants against a pre-agreed 95% target. What is the conclusion?
A prototype volunteer sample excludes users needing assistive technology. What should be added to the acceptance plan?
options: A claim that all users will succeed
A lower target set after testing
Representative accessibility testing and a limitation note
questions.explanation: The sample omits an important use context.

questions.question: The sponsor is unavailable and the team has only a draft charter. What can the coordinator accurately claim?
options: The proposal is prepared; authorisation is pending
questions.explanation: Preparation and approval are different states.

questions.question: A project team disbands after launch. Who should have been assigned to monitor staff-hour savings?
options: The software tool without a responsible role
An operational benefits owner with a review date
No one because launch proves savings
questions.explanation: Benefits often materialise after project closure.

questions.question: A weekly sponsor meeting receives raw task lists but no choices. What is the highest-value redesign?
options: Replace the meeting with a colour alone
Summarise evidence, options and decisions due
Invite more observers without changing content
questions.explanation: Communication should support the recipient’s decisions.
